stops.name: Hraunfossar
stops.detail: The Hraunfossar (from Icelandic [ˈr̥øyːnˌfɔsːar] 'Lava Waterfalls') are waterfalls into the river Hvítá near the towns of Húsafell and Reykholt in western Iceland.

stops.name: Barnafoss
stops.detail: In the immediate vicinity of the Hraunfossar is the Barnafoss waterfall.

stops.name: Hallmundarhraun
stops.detail: Over a length of about 700 meters, foaming and bubbling water flows in over a hundred small waterfalls from the black rock of the approx. 1,000-year-old Hallmundarhraun lava field.

stops.name: Gráhraun
stops.detail: The river named Hvitá, fed by the Langjökull glacier, digs its riverbed along the edge of the Gráhraun lava flow belonging to the Hallmundarhraun, which came to a stop there.

stops.name: Schlucht
stops.detail: A pedestrian bridge leads over the foaming Hvítá river in the small gorge.
